messages:
Maya (AE): OrchID Health (Mike) asking about Private Deploy POC. They prefer PrivateLink/interface endpoints and need static egress IPs for their allowlist. Also concerned about TLS-inspect proxy and monthly delta on pricing.
Mike_CorpIT: Yes, avoid VPC peering if possible. Our security team will proxy-terminate TLS for inspection. We need specifics on ports, cert handling, and whether Redwood can provide stable egress IPs.
Priya (NetOps): PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is fine. We surface service FQDNs via interface endpoints; traffic stays in the customer VPC to ENIs. For egress to Redwood-managed connectors we can allocate dedicated EIPs so you can whitelist concrete IPv4s. Typical outbound is TCP/443. If your proxy terminates TLS, ensure CONNECT to target FQDN is allowed.
Sam (Infra Eng): Patterns we support: 
1) Customer VPC -> Interface Endpoint -> Connector in your VPC (we can run connectors in your account) with assigned EIP(s) so source IP is preserved. 
2) Customer VPC -> Interface Endpoint -> our managed connector in Redwood account (we NAT to our EIPs). 
If source IP preservation is required we recommend option 1 or we manage HA NAT pair for you. For POC, option 2 is faster to stand up.
Maya (AE): Procurement question: what does the connector/EIP management cost add to Dedicated pricing? Ballpark monthly uplift?
Sam (Infra Eng): Connector management fee varies by level of ops involvement. Ballpark: 10%-20% of a small Dedicated reservation for a basic managed HA pair, up to 25% for fully-managed with 24x7 support. EIP cloud charges are passed-through (depends on region and allocation hours). I'll follow up with a formal quote.
Lena (Security): Compliance notes: 
- Control plane requires mTLS for long-term deployments; for short POCs we can accept a VPN/IP-allowlist and time-limited certs. 
- If you terminate TLS in your proxy, you control leaf certs and logs; Redwood needs an attestation for data handling. 
- Key management: Private Deploy supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / Azure KeyVault) for storage encryption.
Mike_CorpIT: For POC timeline: 6 weeks. US-only data residency. Also need answers for security questionnaire Q12-Q16 (KMS, cert rotation, audit logs).
Lena (Security): I'll DM a short skeleton for Q12-Q16. Quick answers: AWS KMS supported, customer-managed CMKs supported on Private Deploy, control-plane cert rotation automated when Redwood manages connectors; when customer terminates TLS at proxy, customer rotates leaf certs. Audit logs: we can provide connector audit events and request logs; retention varies by plan.
Priya (NetOps): Quick network checklist for your ops team: 
- Create interface endpoint(s) for service FQDN(s) in desired AZs
- Update route tables to point to endpoint ENIs
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to the connector EIP(s) or to your proxy IPs
- For TLS-inspect proxies, allow CONNECT and SNI passthrough (if using passthrough, avoid MITM of Redwood certs)
- Provide preferred AZs and any ASN for BGP if doing transit options

Sam (Infra Eng): Example firewall snippet for your team to paste: 
```
# Allowlist for Redwood POC connectors
ALLOW OUT tcp 443 -> 198.51.100.12,198.51.100.13
# If using interface endpoint ENIs (VPC-local)
ALLOW OUT tcp 443 -> 10.10.5.0/28  # endpoint ENIs
```

Maya (AE): Next steps: Sam to prepare a written quote and EIP count options, Priya to share a more detailed network handoff doc, Lena to send the security questionnaire skeleton. Mike, I'll schedule a kickoff and include procurement and netsec. :thumbsup:
Mike_CorpIT: Sounds good. Please include a minimal checklist for the POC that our firewall team can action in one week.
